absent: Full semantics of in-kernel versus user irqchip, LAPIC, and controller helpers and of vendor callbacks for shadows, masks, virtual NMI, clock, and machine-check setup.
Complete ioctl dispatch beyond the truncated part one, including debug-register tail, remaining cases, and error precedence.
Exact numeric values, bit positions, and widths of ABI constants, request identifiers, valid-bit masks, and machine-check status bits.
Concrete C layouts, sizes, alignment, and padding of user structures and per-vCPU arch state beyond fields observed in use.
Locking context, sleepability, ordering between vCPU loading, reclaim sections, and timestamp lock, and interrupt-state requirements.
Confidential and protected-state handling, floating-point copy helpers, TSC scaling and synchronization, clock-base capture, and paravirtual time activation.
Exception queueing, reinjection, payload quirk, management-mode entry and nested-exit handling, and triple-fault delivery.
Hypervisor enlightenment activation, CPUID enforcement, and direct-flush support beyond gating checks shown.

findings.text: Per-vCPU ioctl dispatcher that resolves the calling vCPU from the file context, marks it loaded for the duration, then branches on the ioctl identifier to per-feature helpers for local APIC state, external interrupt and NMI and SMI injection, CPUID, machine-specific registers, single registers, TPR reporting, virtual APIC address, machine-check setup and injection, event state, and debug registers, translating user-copy failures and helper rejections into negative error returns.
Global helper reporting total pending nonmaskable interrupts as the sum of software-counted pending state and the virtual pending indicator from the vendor layer.

External interrupt injection is accepted only when no external interrupt is already held and, with in-kernel local APIC, the APIC accepts controller interrupts; an interrupt window is reported only when architectural delivery is allowed plus that acceptance plus absence of reinjection need plus absence of pending exception.

Interrupt ioctl validates the vector against the architectural interrupt count, then splits by irqchip placement: without in-kernel irqchip it queues the vector and raises an event request; with in-kernel irqchip it rejects in-kernel controller configurations, rejects a second pending external vector while one is held, otherwise latches the vector and raises an event request. NMI ioctl unconditionally injects and reports success, and TPR reporting ioctl rejects nonzero flags and otherwise stores the enabled state as boolean.

Machine-check setup derives bank count from the low byte of the capability word, requires nonzero count within the maximum and requires capability bits within supported plus reserved masks, otherwise fails; on success it stores the capability, initializes global control to all enabled when control-present is set, initializes each bank control to all enabled and each extended control to disabled when corrected-interrupt capability is set, then notifies local APIC layer and vendor setup hook.

No-action-required is recognized when global status is clear and bank status has valid and uncorrected set while context signalling and address-valid are clear; such reports update status address and miscellaneous slots and global status and, only when corrected-interrupt capability and per-bank enable are both present with in-kernel APIC, deliver a local corrected message, without raising a machine-check exception.

Machine-check injection validates bank index and valid bit, applies speculative-index hardening, diverts no-action-required cases, silently drops uncorrected reports when global or per-bank controls disable reporting, escalates to triple fault when a machine check is already in progress or machine-check enable in control register four is clear, otherwise records address miscellaneous and status with overflow handling and queues a machine-check exception; corrected reports merge with overflow handling and never overwrite an existing uncorrected valid entry except to set overflow.

Event query drains pending nonmaskable and management interrupts, applies a payload compatibility adjustment, clears the output, hides software exceptions from injected and pending reporting while still reporting number error code and payload, conflates pending into injected when payload capability is disabled, reports hardware interrupt state number and shadow, nonmaskable injected pending and mask, management-mode state when built with that feature, latched init, and flag bits advertising which groups are valid including conditional payload and triple-fault validity.

Nonmaskable pending count evolves by folding an atomic queued count into a bounded pending count: limit is one when masked or an injection is outstanding else two, reduced by one when a virtual nonmaskable is pending, then one unit is offered to the virtual mechanism when possible and any remainder raises an event request; total observed by userspace is software pending plus virtual pending, and userspace restore clears software pending and replaces the atomic queued count, raising a nonmaskable request when nonzero.

Event restore rejects unknown valid flags and payload use without payload enablement, normalizes payload and pending interaction, rejects injected or pending vectors beyond the architectural exception range or equal to the nonmaskable vector, drains nonmaskables, marks userspace-originated pending exceptions for later exit morphing while clearing vendor exit state, installs exception interrupt and nonmaskable fields, conditionally updates interrupt shadow and nonmaskable mask, accepts startup vector only with in-kernel APIC, reconciles management-mode transitions with nested exit handling and mode-change notification, manages latched init bit, enforces triple-fault capability gating, and always raises an event request.

Extended-save query copies only guest-enabled features plus always-allowed floating and vector state and fails or returns empty for confidential guests depending on protected-state presence; update clears extended-disable bits from the backup bitmap for compatibility before delegating with host-supported mask and protection-key state; control-register query returns empty when host lacks save support else a single enabled-mask entry and update validates count flags and host support, honors only the enabled-mask entry through the internal setter, and normalizes failures.

Counter device attributes support only the offset attribute within the counter control group, rejecting other groups or attributes; presence check reports availability, readback returns the level-one offset, update consumes a user offset, scales current counter by the level-one ratio, captures clock base, evaluates a same-frequency same-offset fast-path hint, and synchronizes under the timestamp write lock.

Guest-paused marking requires active paravirtual time and then flags stopped state with a clock-update request; capability enabling rejects nonzero flags and dispatches synthetic-controller activation gated on in-kernel irqchip with zero-argument enforcement for the second version, enlightened-structure activation gated on nested support with version returned to user, direct flush gated on vendor support, and enforcement toggles for hypervisor and paravirtual CPUID, rejecting unknown identifiers.

Timestamp offset update serializes against concurrent updates with the per-VM timestamp write lock held with interrupts saved across scaling base capture and synchronization; virtual-APIC address programming and event-state restore execute under a reclaim read-side critical section acquired around the update.

Bank index from userspace must be speculation-hardened before use as an array selector; every user-pointer copy can fail and must propagate a fault without partial state change; restoring events conflates pending and injected when payload is disabled and can spuriously convert an injected exception into a pending one subject to interception; uncorrected errors during an in-progress machine check or with machine-check enable clear escalate to triple fault rather than queuing another exception.

Interrupt vector acceptance is bounded by limit KVM_NR_INTERRUPTS and machine-check setup bank count is bounded by limit KVM_MAX_MCE_BANKS, with distinct rejections for invalid argument, duplicate external vector, and in-kernel controller unsupported case.

Valid-bit mask uses KVM_VCPUEVENT_VALID_NMI_PENDING, KVM_VCPUEVENT_VALID_SIPI_VECTOR, KVM_VCPUEVENT_VALID_SHADOW, KVM_VCPUEVENT_VALID_SMM, KVM_VCPUEVENT_VALID_PAYLOAD, KVM_VCPUEVENT_VALID_TRIPLE_FAULT.

Counter control uses group KVM_VCPU_TSC_CTRL with attribute KVM_VCPU_TSC_OFFSET; event processing uses requests KVM_REQ_EVENT, KVM_REQ_NMI, KVM_REQ_TRIPLE_FAULT and, when built with management-mode support, KVM_REQ_SMI.

User layouts observed include kvm_interrupt with irq; kvm_tpr_access_ctl with flags and enabled; kvm_x86_mce with bank status addr misc and global status; kvm_vcpu_events with exception interrupt nmi smi triple-fault flags and payloads; kvm_xcrs with count flags and entries of selector plus value.
